hypothesis: Refine the endpoint-validation-hoisting proposal with direct recognition of the status field grammar. A valid status is exactly zero or more leading ASCII zeroes followed by [1-5][0-9][0-9] and TAB, so status arithmetic and the per-digit upper-bound loop can be replaced by direct byte checks while preserving every accepted spelling. Combined with validating each new endpoint once using char::is_control, this removes redundant parsing work on repeated and distinct endpoints. Round-3 development data reduced the Unicode-endpoint cost from round-2 roughly 92-105 ns/record to roughly 64-76, but remaining ASCII repeated-key costs around 55-65 ns/record and essentially unchanged high-cardinality costs leave plausible common-path headroom. Direct status recognition applies to all records rather than a workload-size threshold.
notes: Fresh model-authored final proposal; static inspection only, no compile/test/benchmark by the proposal author. The actual accepted base is round 2. Round 3 passed correctness and had favorable development timing, but was not promoted because its uncertainty lower bound narrowly missed the prespecified 1.05x gate. This full-file proposal retains that unaccepted endpoint mechanism and adds exact status-grammar recognition; the combined improvement is unmeasured and is not claimed to clear the gate. No thresholds or repetitions are being changed to reverse the prior decision. Status 000100..000599 remains accepted, including arbitrarily many leading zeroes; statuses below 100, above 599, signs, overflow-sized nonzero values, extra digits and non-ASCII spellings remain rejected. Byte-count arithmetic, line endings, field count and output sorting remain unchanged. Standard randomized hashing and its seed variability remain. Risks inherited from endpoint validation hoisting include less reuse for unique keys and hashing numerically valid rows with invalid endpoint controls before rejection. Leading-zero-heavy status strings still require a linear scan; performance gains may be smaller than expected without profiling. No unsafe code, global caching, extra dependencies or case-specific paths.
